open_points.subject: answer_request response id
open_points.text: answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
open_points.other_text: answer_request: [FIELD_PROJECTION] The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
open_points.question: For a body rejected by the first size check, must the body remain unread and the response id be null, or must it be parsed to preserve its string or integer id?

open_points.subject: translate_failure reason disclosure
open_points.text: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] Text an agent supplies — purposes, implementation code, names — is data: it is never evaluated, imported, compiled, formatted or interpreted in the kernel process; a JSON text it supplies is data too, parsed only as JSON by canonical_bytes and by the schema check of the module that judges it, never evaluated or executed; no answer and no refusal carries a token, a service credential, a host path or a stack trace, an internal error included (A16 rules 5 and 7).
open_points.other_text: translate_failure: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] The reason of every code but internal_error is the exception's own message cut to at most the imported RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX constant bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary; internal_error carries an empty reason, never the exception text, type, path or stack trace (A16 rule 7).
open_points.question: When a non-internal exception's own message contains a token, service credential, host path or stack trace, must that message be preserved except for truncation, or sanitized to satisfy the disclosure prohibition?

open_points.subject: serve_kernel startup error reporting
open_points.text: run_start_sequence: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Every step is required: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller, the same exception with its own reason; before it propagates MUST write the failing step's name — load_installation, check_installed_instances, open_store, probe_sandbox, recover_in_flight_attempts or recover_running_runs — as one line to standard error, so the step is named there and the reason stays the exception's own; no later step runs and nothing is retried or skipped.
open_points.other_text: serve_kernel: [VALIDATION_ERROR] When run_start_sequence raises, which has already written the failing step's name, MUST write the exception's reason to standard error, without any token, credential value, configuration content or stack trace, open no entrance and return a non-zero exit code; there is no partial start and no retry.
open_points.question: When the unchanged reason of a startup exception contains a token, credential value, configuration content or stack trace, must serve_kernel write that reason verbatim or redact it?
